name: Mucocele of Paranasal Sinuses

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Paranasal Sinus Mucocele

criteria.description: Presence of progressive facial swelling or deformity localized to the affected sinus region
CT or MRI evidence of an expansile, cystic lesion causing sinus opacification with bone erosion or remodeling
Evidence of sinus ostium obstruction or prior sinus surgery/trauma history

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological confirmation is rarely required unless malignancy is suspected

common.symptomName: Proptosis or displacement of the eye

laboratory: Generally normal; inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated if secondary infection present
imaging: CT scan showing expansile, homogenous cystic lesion with thinning or erosion of sinus walls
MRI demonstrating fluid-filled lesion with variable signal intensity depending on content
other: Endoscopic examination may reveal mucosal swelling or obstruction of sinus ostium

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of mucosal thickening without cystic expansion
Presence of infection with purulent content

redFlags: Visual disturbances including diplopia or vision loss
Signs of intracranial extension such as severe headache or neurological deficits
references: Som PM, Curtin HD. Head and Neck Imaging. 5th ed. Elsevier; 2011.
Kennedy DW. Functional endoscopic sinus surgery. Technique. Arch Otolaryngol. 1985;111(10):643-649.
Lund VJ, Stammberger H, et al. European Position Paper on Rhinosinusitis and Nasal Polyps 2020.
